### 2. At the frozen moment: act, wait or refuse

The answer is to act now, as a chain (the waiver is not grantable at the opening; see item 6).
Visible eligibility grounds for the waiver (ledger credits standard §C and the allowance table):
- Tenure. find_leases shows `move_in_date 2022-10-15`, floor plan `One-Bedroom Den Residence`. Allowance table: "Minimum full calendar months since move-in | 6". 41 full months have passed on 2026-03-22, so this passes.
- Courtesy waivers used in the trailing 365 days: the lease's waiver credits (`late_fee_waiver`) are all dated `2025-02-20`, which is outside 2025-03-22..2026-03-22. That is 0 used against "Courtesy waivers available within the trailing 365 days | 1", so this passes.
- Autopay. The allowance table says "ACH autopay enrollment required | Yes" for One-Bedroom Den, and find_leases shows `autopay_enrolled: True`. Passes.
- find_lease_payments shows no NSF, account-closed or stop-payment return. Status is `active`, not eviction filed. Both pass.
- Hub gate (courtesy waiver posting card): "A courtesy waiver on a billing period is granted only after the ledger shows a catch-up payment for that period, received on or after its first late day, in the full catch-up amount." At the opening, the only March payment is `debit_card 700.0 2026-03-12`, which is not the full catch-up amount. The waiver is therefore not grantable until the prerequisites are resolved.

### 4. Scored parameters

**(a) Preferred employer discount credit for 2026-03.**
Computation document ("Preferred Employer Discount Credit Amount"): "the preferred employer rate times the amount of the period's base rent line, rounded half up to the cent. The preferred employer rate is the floor plan's preferred employer discount rate." The floor plan rate is 0.05 ("One-Bedroom Den Residence | 0 (none) | 12 months | 0.05 (5%)").
Factors found from the records:
- Autopay-draft step ("Training Note — Autopay Drafts and the Preferred Employer Rate"). find_lease_payments shows `ach_autopay` payments dated 2025-04-01..2026-02-01. That is 11 in the window after 2025-03-22. "10 or more | 0.005" gives +0.005. Found with the record word "ACH autopay" (KB_search "ACH autopay drafts" ranks it first).
- Household step ("Household Parking and Storage Step"). find_parking_licenses shows `Covered Carport Space status active`, and find_storage_rentals shows `Standard Storage Unit (5x5) status active`. "Yes | Yes | 0.005" gives +0.005. Found with "parking license storage rental" (ranks first).
- Renewal step ("Preferred Employer Rate — Renewal History Step"). find_term_rent_changes shows three records with `change_reason: renewal`. "3 or more | 0.010" gives +0.010.
- Tenure step ("Residency Length Step on the Preferred Employer Rate"). Move-in 2022-10-15 gives 41 full months on 2026-03-22. "36 to 47 | 0.0025" gives +0.0025.
- Rate: 0.05 + 0.005 + 0.005 + 0.010 + 0.0025 = 0.0725. Discount: 0.0725 × 1980.00 = 143.55, rounded half up, which is 143.55.
- Late-month factor ("Preferred Employer Credit for a Month Whose Rent Went Late"). The March period carries an initial late fee line. The other initial late fee line is 2025-02-05, which falls outside "after 2025-03-22". The row "Yes | No | three quarters (75%) | down to the cent" applies: 143.55 × 0.75 = 107.6625, rounded down to **107.66**.
- Fall-back (computation document plus the rate table only): 0.05 × 1980.00 = **99.00**. That is definite and differs from 107.66.

**(b) Catch-up amount (paid by the customer).**

- recurring fees = 99.00
- late fees = 195.00 less waivers/reversals (none) = 195.00
- payments = received after 2026-02-22 through 2026-03-22, which is the 700.00 of 2026-03-12
Factors:
- Application order ("Order of Application for a Late Month's Payments"). There is no payment return in the last 12 months, and there are renewal rent changes (3). Row "No | 1 or more | rent, late fees, recurring fees" applies. The 700.00 goes to rent, leaving rent unpaid 1172.34, late fees unpaid 195.00 and recurring fees unpaid 99.00.
- Late fees carried ("Apartment Home Lease Catch-Up Amounts — Late Fees Carried"). No other billing period has an initial late fee line dated after 2025-03-22. "0 | $0.00", so 0.00 is carried.
- Recurring fees carried ("Training Note — Recurring Fees in a Catch-Up Amount"). There are 11 ACH autopay payments in the last 12 months. "10 or more | none", so 0.00.
- Next month's rent ("Next Month's Rent in a Catch-Up Amount"). There are 41 full months in possession. "36 or more | never", so 0.00, even though 2026-03-22 is 10 days before 2026-04-01 and the baseline window would have added 1980.00.

With the credit posted: payments 700 go to fees 99, then late 195, then rent 406. Rent unpaid is 1466.34, plus 1980.00, giving **3446.34**. That is definite and differs.

**(c) Courtesy waiver amount.**
Computation document ("Courtesy Waiver Amount"): "the period's covered late fees times the waiver share, rounded half up to the cent. The period's covered late fees are all of its late fee lines, and the waiver share is the whole of them."
Factors:
- Covered lines ("Courtesy Waiver Coverage of Late Fee Lines"). The courtesy waiver credits already on record, at any date, are 96 + 5×12 = 156.00, which lands in the ">0 and ≤250" row. That covers the initial line plus 5 daily lines at the average daily amount (10.00): 95.00 + 50.00 = 145.00.

- Fall-back (computation document only): 195.00 × 1 = **195.00**. That is definite and differs.

### 6. The problem tree derived from visible materials alone

The root problem is the courtesy waiver on 2026-03, which the customer asked for.

- **Hop 1 (waiver ← catch-up payment): state-derived.**
  - The waiver hub says: "A courtesy waiver on a billing period is granted only after the ledger shows a catch-up payment for that period, received on or after its first late day, in the full catch-up amount."
  - The records show only the 700.00 debit-card payment, so the state does not hold.
  - Searching the sentence's words ("catch-up payment") finds "Rent Catch-Up Payment — Apartment Home Lease Resident Portal Terms" (KB_search "catch-up payment amount", rank 1). That document describes the write that brings the state about: a "one-time lease payment that brings the most recent late billing period ... current, and its amount is the catch-up amount". It is the customer's own tool.
- **Hop 2 (catch-up payment ← employer credit): state-derived.**
  - The catch-up document says: "The catch-up amount for a late billing period is not fixed until that period's base rent line carries the preferred employer discount credit owed on a lease enrolled in the preferred employer program."
  - The records show `rent_discount_program: preferred_employer`, and the 2026-03 base rent line `690a0629` has no `preferred_employer_discount` credit (unlike every earlier month), so the state does not hold.
  - The words "preferred employer discount credit" find "Preferred Employer Discount Credit — Ledger Posting Card". It says the credit "is owed for every billing period of a lease enrolled ... whose base rent line carries no preferred employer discount credit" and "is posted as one preferred employer discount credit whose source charge is that base rent line". That is the write.
  - No concession credit is present on March, so the credit is owed.
- **Nothing further.** The employer posting card states no prerequisite. The late fee review card was checked too. The March lines reproduce the review schedule:
  - clock Mon 03-02, grace 3 + 2 (tenure ≥ 36 months), first late day 03-08
  - review percentage 0.040 (no earlier late period in the 6-month look-back from 3 renewal changes, no return), so the initial fee is max(95, 79.20) = 95.00
  - daily fee 12 − 2 = 10.00 (12-month term)
  - 10 lines (capped); accrual end = the handling date, since there is no submitted plan request (the only request is `completed`) and no notice
  - The total is 195.00 against a cap of 237.60, so the lines "stand as posted" and no reversal is owed. No write is needed there.
- Order: (1) employer credit (agent), then (2) catch-up payment (customer), then (3) courtesy waiver (agent).
- No hop is pre-solved. No document of the waiver names the catch-up tool or the employer-credit tool, and no route, chain or aggregated list appears. Each blocked hub names only its own tool.

### Two-way counter-proof

- **"Do only the thing asked" (post the waiver now).** The hub sentence says it is "granted only after the ledger shows a catch-up payment ... in the full catch-up amount", and the gating table row "No such payment | not granted" rules it out. The ledger shows only 700.00. Excluded by visible text and records.
- **Paying the catch-up before the employer credit.** "a figure worked out while the late period's base rent line carries no preferred employer discount credit is not yet the catch-up amount". Excluded.
- **Computing the waiver before the catch-up payment.** Then the latest payment would be 2026-03-12 (10 days, whole share) and the waiver would be 145.00. That is not the order the hub allows, because the waiver comes only after the payment. Once the payment lands, the latest payment date is 2026-03-22, which gives 20 days and 0.80. Excluded by order.
- **Clock on 2026-03-01.** That would give 21 days and 0.60, so a waiver of 145 × 0.70 = 101.50. Excluded by the lateness-clock document: "when no such draft was returned and the due date fell on a Saturday or a Sunday the clock starts on the following Monday". 2026-03-01 is a Sunday.
- **Covering all lines (195.00).** Excluded because the coverage factor reads the 156.00 of prior waivers on record "for every period and at any date".
- **Credit rounding.** Half up to 107.67 is excluded by "rounded down to the cent" in the 75% row.
- **Next-month rent in the catch-up.** Excluded by the 36+ month row "never".
- **Late-fee-review reversal as an extra step.** Excluded because the posted lines equal the review schedule (item 6), so the review result is "the lines stand as posted".
